title: Catalog activation campaign tactical checklist for a new model addition
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Operational checklist to coordinate cross-team go-to-market work for adding a new model to the catalog. Covers benchmark gating, documentation artifacts, release notes, announcement cadence, dashboard readiness and stakeholder comms. This ticket binds owners across Eng, Design, Docs, Support, and Marketing and tracks end-to-end tasks and acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Model listed in catalog with metadata and trimmed description
Benchmark suite published and passing threshold for latency and quality
User-facing docs (Quickstart + API examples) live in docs site and reviewed by PM + Eng
Release notes drafted, approved, and scheduled in release pipeline
Marketing announcement assets ready and scheduled with comms calendar
Console dashboards reflect new model and cost/latency baselines
tasks: 1) Catalog metadata: gather model name, tags, input/output types, recommended prompts, and cost guidance — owner: PM (Liam Chen)
2) Benchmarks: run standard suite (latency p50/p95, token cost, quality evals) and upload results to shared dashboard — owner: Eng (Priya Rao)
3) Docs: write Quickstart, SDK snippet, and migration notes; submit PR to docs repo and request review — owner: Docs (Sofia Martinez)
4) Release notes: draft entry with breaking changes, upgrade path, and known limitations; get legal and security sign-off — owner: PM (Aisha Kumar)
5) Console: add model tile, default route configs, and tracing hooks; verify observability panels — owner: Eng (Mateo Alvarez)
6) Design: craft product screenshots and assets for marketing and docs — owner: Design (Elena Park)
7) Marketing: prepare announcement copy, blog draft, and social posts; align publish window with legal/regional constraints — owner: Marketing (Noah Patel)
8) Support enablement: create internal KB, triage guide and sample prompts for common issues — owner: Support (Riley Thompson)
9) Rollout plan: define canary cohort, rollout % increments and rollback conditions — owner: PM + Eng
10) Compliance: confirm data handling, KMS keys, and audit logging for private deployments if target customers require — owner: Security
stakeholders: Product: Aisha Kumar (PM Lead), Liam Chen (PM)

notes: Tactical play: staggered announcement — internal preview to existing dedicated customers two business days before public blog. Canary rollout limited to 5% traffic for first 48h, then 25% if no regressions.
risk_mitigation: Fallback route: if latency regression observed, auto-rollover to smaller model variant and pause public rollout
Monitoring: create dedicated alert for token cost spikes and QoE regressions tied to new model
Support ramp: schedule a 30-minute readiness sync with Support on day 0 and provide triage playbook
